note: Window agent m2500-m2401. keyframe_overrides/0 and /1 keep the Sumer hegemonies of Ur (-2500) and Lagash (-2450) on the Euphrates-Tigris alluvium (the gazetteer's Sumer admin-1 provinces run about 380 cells into the western desert). events/0 gives Umma its own 11 cells (the succession rule had left it one). events/1 (month 12 so that it follows sumerian-city-states/ledger/7) returns Lagash its 50 km core after -2425, which the collective's gain had swallowed.

events.note: 2500 BCE: Umma draws its own cells. The Umma page lists a dynasty 'c. 2500-2230 BC' (Pabilgagaltuku, Ush, Enakalle, Ur-Lumma) and calls Umma 'Best known for its long frontier conflict with Lagash'. Mirror of sumerian-city-states/ledger/5 (Lagash): without a split the compiler's succession rule (R2, umma's successor is sumerian-city-states) gave the ten cells of Umma's own 30 km disk to the collective for the whole life of Umma, leaving it one cell.

region.text: Lagash, Girsu, Nina and the Gu-edena

events.note: 2425 BCE: Lagash stays a state under Enannatum I (r. c. 2425 BC) and Entemena ('increased the power of Lagash during his rule', r. c. 2420 BC) until Urukagina is 'defeated by Lugalzagesi' (r. c. 2350 BC): 'the Lagash state incorporated the cities of Lagash, Girsu, and Nina'. sumerian-city-states/ledger/7 takes back 'Sumer apart from Umma and Ur', a region that contains Lagash's own disk, so the state was left with no land from -2425 to its end; this returns the 50 km core of keyframe lagash_-2425.

correction.text: Mesannepada's hegemony over Sumer drawn on the alluvial plain only: the gazetteer's Sumer region intersected with Cliopatria's -2500 Sumerian city-states outline, without Lagash (40 km) and Umma (30 km)

keyframe_overrides.why: The Sumer page puts the Sumerian cities 'in the Euphrates-Tigris alluvial plain, south of Baghdad' with Eridu 'on the coast of the Persian Gulf'; the First Dynasty of Ur page says only that the dynasty 'had extensive influence over the area of Sumer, and apparently led a union of south Mesopotamian polities'. The admin-1 'Sumer' region (Dhi-Qar, Al-Muthannia, Al-Qadisiyyah, ...) adds about 380 cells of western desert that Cliopatria's outline and the sumerian-city-states keyframe do not hold.

correction.text: Eannatum's hegemony 'all of Sumer' drawn on the alluvial plain only: the gazetteer's Sumer region intersected with Cliopatria's -2500 Sumerian city-states outline, without Umma (30 km, vassal) and Ur (40 km, occupied)

keyframe_overrides.why: Same ground as first-dynasty-of-ur_-2500: Eannatum 'annexed practically all of Sumer, including Kish' (Sumer page), and Sumer lies in the 'Euphrates-Tigris alluvial plain, south of Baghdad'; the whole admin-1 Sumer region would draw him over Al-Muthannia desert that no page assigns to any city.
